title: Canonical finite smooth coefficient and twist arrows
statement: Let A→B be a homomorphism of finite commutative coefficient rings, N and M natural numbers annihilating A and B (in the quotient application they are positive and M divides N), and f:X→Y compactifiable. Use the canonical maps, comparison functors, source and exceptional transport of [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. Scalar extension S_T is the left adjoint to actual derived restriction [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]; its site comparison is the canonical mate [def-weil-pbc-witness-compatibility]. Define normalized root-line comparison data by: a map mu_N→mu_M whose inclusion into G_m is raising to N/M, a scalar-extension sheaf isomorphism of the actual finite root lines [def-pur-roots-of-unity-sheaf] and [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] sending every scalar/root generator a tensor z to phi(a) tensor z^(N/M), and a derived isomorphism equal to the canonical scalar counit followed by that sheaf isomorphism. Define its d-fold shifted tensor comparison recursively using the canonical scalar unit at zero, the representative-normalized tensor comparison, and shift commutation. Define lambda_0 by scalar/tensor balancing, scalar/pullback balancing, and this root-line comparison. Reuse b and c from [lem-pur-exceptional-coefficient-comparison], where b is the open/proper compactification map and c is the actual counit transpose. Define the origin/scalar map by adjunction from the inverse site/scalar comparison followed by the scalar-extended origin counit. Transport c using this map and the site/scalar comparison to define c_pro on the fixed pro-etale complexes. Transport the pure pullback balancing map and the root-line map through the site/scalar comparison to define their pro-etale arrows. Transport lambda_0 using the same origin counit and source comparisons to define lambda_pro. Transport b using those same origin counits and the canonical open/proper site comparison to define b_pro. Define b_pro inverse by its inverse on its isomorphism locus and zero elsewhere. No isomorphism, compatibility or cocycle is assumed by these definitions; those are conclusions of finite smooth purity. QuotientCocycle is notation for t_23(c_12(K)) followed by c_23(s_12(K)) and F_3(a_K) equalling b_(F_1 K) followed by c_13(K), where a and b are the actual scalar associators at the source and target. Applications instantiate every functor and comparison with the canonical operations just specified.
